beats.text: You hit send. Your message becomes light.
It is chopped into dozens of packets, each carrying its own address.
Routers fire them hop by hop, choosing the best path in microseconds.
Packets take different roads and arrive out of order. Scrambled is fine.
TCP numbers every piece and rebuilds your message at the end.
Lost one? TCP just asks for it again. No drama.
Trillions of times a second, this is the heartbeat of the internet.

scenes.caption: every packet knows where it belongs
